title: From sites to structure to serology: a roadmap for structure-aware molecular evolution of antigenically evolving viruses.

analysis.background: The massive influx of viral genome sequences has driven the field toward site‑resolved molecular evolution.
analysis.main_directions: For antigenically evolving viruses such as influenza and SARS‑CoV‑2, dense sampling enables mutation‑annotated phylogenies, while structure‑aware phylogenetic and machine‑learning tools map mutations onto three‑dimensional constraints and predict antigenic outcomes.
analysis.current_state: Evidence shows that sequence context, genomic region, RNA structure, and protein‑level constraints strongly shape substitution patterns, and antigenic cartography now links genetic change to epidemiologically relevant antigenic distance.
analysis.gaps: The divergence between genetic and antigenic “clocks” remains poorly understood, limiting the ability to predict immune escape from sequence data alone.
analysis.future_research: A practical framework linking sites, structure, and serology is proposed, and integrating genomic surveillance, phylogenetics, structural analysis, and predictive modeling is recommended to improve prospective variant assessment and vaccine design.

analysis.summary_en: Background: The massive influx of viral genome sequences has driven the field toward site‑resolved molecular evolution. Main directions: Dense sampling of influenza and SARS‑CoV‑2 supports mutation‑annotated phylogenies, while structure‑aware phylogenetics and machine‑learning map mutations onto 3D constraints and predict antigenic change. Current state: Sequence context, RNA structure, and protein constraints strongly influence substitution patterns, and antigenic cartography translates genetic change into antigenic distance. Gaps: The divergence between genetic and antigenic clocks is not yet resolved. Future research: Implement a framework linking sites, structure, and serology, and integrate surveillance, phylogenetics, structural analysis, and predictive modeling to enhance variant assessment and vaccine design.

title: Does diagnosis by biopsy versus serology‐only affect follow‐up in celiac disease?

analysis.background: Serology‑only diagnosis of celiac disease is increasing, but few recent studies have examined patient outcomes (A1).
analysis.methods: Patients with TTG IgA ≥10 × upper limit of normal diagnosed between 1 Oct 2020 and 30 Sep 2022 at Seattle Children’s Hospital and followed for 2 years were included; symptoms, GI and dietitian visit timing/number, TTG IgA, HLA status, and endoscopy results were recorded and analyzed with t‑test, Wilcoxon rank‑sum, and chi‑square (A3‑A7).
analysis.results: Fifty‑four patients (mean age 9.7 ± 4.3 y) were studied; 32 (59%) diagnosed by biopsy and 22 (41%) by serology‑only (A8‑A10). Baseline TTG IgA titers were similar and declined in both groups with no significant differences at any time point (A11‑A12). Mean time to first dietitian visit, number of dietitian visits, and total dietitian visits over 24 months were also not significantly different (A13).
analysis.contribution: The study indicates that serology‑only diagnosis leads to comparable clinical follow‑up frequency and TTG IgA reduction as biopsy diagnosis, supporting non‑invasive diagnostic pathways (A14).
analysis.limitations: Only abstract data are available, limiting detail on methodology, full statistical results, and generalizability; the study is single‑center with a modest sample size (A8).

analysis.summary_en: Background: Serology-only diagnosis of celiac disease is increasing, yet outcomes are understudied. Methods: A retrospective cohort of patients with TTG IgA ≥10× ULN diagnosed between Oct 2020–Sep 2022 at Seattle Children’s Hospital and followed for 2 years recorded symptoms, GI and dietitian visits, TTG IgA, HLA, and endoscopy, analyzed with t‑test, Wilcoxon, and chi‑square. Results: Fifty‑four patients (mean age 9.7 ± 4.3 y); 32 biopsy, 22 serology-only; baseline TTG IgA similar and declined similarly; no significant differences in dietitian visit timing or number (p > 0.05). Contribution: Suggests serology-only diagnosis yields comparable follow‑up and serologic response to biopsy, supporting non‑invasive pathways. Limitations: Only abstract data provided, limiting methodological detail; single‑center, modest sample size.

title: Proof-of-Concept Development and Preclinical Evaluation of a Microarray Patch Platform for Codelivery of Multiple Broadly Neutralizing Antibodies for HIV Prevention.

analysis.background: Broadly neutralizing antibodies (bnAbs) are promising for HIV prevention or treatment but currently require invasive parenteral injection, which is especially problematic for pediatric use (A1).
analysis.methods: Proof‑of‑concept microneedle (MN) patches were fabricated by solvent casting, each 1 cm² pixel containing ~2 mg of a bnAb (A2, A3). Ex vivo porcine skin tests assessed penetration (A4); in vitro PBS dissolution measured release kinetics (A5); in vitro HIV‑1 neutralization assays evaluated antibody functionality (A6); and a rat model examined pharmacokinetics after co‑administration of three 1 cm² patches (A7).
analysis.results: MN patches penetrated porcine skin and fully dissolved within 10 min (A4, A5). VRC07‑523LS and PGT121 retained neutralizing activity, whereas PGDM1400LS lost some potency (A6). In rats, systemic exposure was detectable by 3 h and peaked by day 3 at concentrations up to 68 µg/mL (A7).
analysis.contribution: The study suggests MN patches could replace injectable bnAb formulations, offering a minimally invasive, potentially cold‑chain‑free delivery suitable for neonates, infants, and resource‑limited settings (A8, A9).
analysis.limitations: Findings are limited to preclinical proof‑of‑concept data; clinical efficacy, safety, and long‑term stability were not evaluated, and only an abstract is available (A8).

analysis.summary_en: Background: bnAbs need invasive injection, limiting pediatric use (A1). Methods: Microneedle patches (~2 mg per 1 cm² pixel) were fabricated and tested for skin penetration, rapid dissolution, antibody functionality, and rat pharmacokinetics (A2‑A7). Results: Patches penetrated skin, dissolved within 10 min, retained activity for two bnAbs (loss for one), and achieved up to 68 µg/mL in rats by day 3 (A4‑A7). Contribution: Provides a minimally invasive, cold‑chain‑free delivery option for HIV prevention, especially for infants and low‑resource settings (A8, A9). Limitations: Preclinical proof‑of‑concept only; no clinical data; abstract only (A8).

title: In silico design and validation of high-affinity RNA aptamers for SARS-CoV-2 comparable to neutralizing antibodies.

analysis.background: Nucleic acid aptamers hold promise for clinical use, yet understanding their molecular binding mechanisms and efficiently optimizing their affinities remain challenging.
analysis.methods: The authors present CAAMO, a computational pipeline that determines aptamer–RBD binding modes, applies structure‑based rational design, and integrates in silico mutagenesis and energy calculations.
analysis.results: Among six designed RNA aptamers, five were experimentally verified and showed enhanced binding affinity compared with the original Ta sequence; the optimized aptamer TaG34C exhibited binding affinity to the SARS‑CoV‑2 RBD comparable to representative neutralizing antibodies.
analysis.contribution: The work provides a robust approach for rapidly generating high‑affinity, complex‑topology aptamers, highlighting their potential as antibody alternatives and enabling RNA‑based diagnostics and therapeutics.
analysis.limitations: Quantitative affinity values, in‑vivo efficacy data, and detailed experimental protocols are not reported in the supplied evidence.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Nucleic acid aptamers hold promise but their binding mechanisms and affinity optimization are challenging. Methods: CAAMO integrates computational modeling, structure‑based design, and in silico mutagenesis to optimize aptamers for the SARS‑CoV‑2 RBD. Results: Five of six designed aptamers showed enhanced binding, and TaG34C matched neutralizing antibody affinity. Contribution: This provides a rapid, robust platform for antibody‑like aptamers and supports RNA‑based diagnostics and therapeutics. Limitations: Quantitative affinity data, in‑vivo validation, and detailed methods are not reported.

title: Detection, virus isolation, and phylogenetic analysis of PRRSV2 in China from 2022 to 2025.

analysis.background: PRRS is a major threat to the global pig industry, and in China the circulating PRRSV2 genotype 2 comprises lineages 1, 3, 5, and 8, with sublineages 1.5 (NADC34-like) and 1.8 (NADC30-like) being prominent.
analysis.methods: Nationwide surveillance from 2022‑2025 collected 23,962 samples; qRT‑PCR detected PRRSV2; 389 isolates were obtained in porcine alveolar macrophage cells, 59 of which replicated in Marc‑145 cells; 79 genomes were sequenced and phylogenetic analysis was performed on the ORF5 gene.

analysis.contribution: The study supplies current prevalence data, identifies dominant strain types, and reveals extensive recombination, thereby supporting molecular epidemiology, surveillance, and vaccine strategy development for PRRSV2 in China.
analysis.limitations: No limitations were reported in the supplied evidence.

title: Immune Mechanisms and Translational Study Design in Viral Vaccine Development.

analysis.background: Viral vaccine development requires mechanistic understanding of protective immunity and translational study designs that connect preclinical data with human outcomes. (A1)
analysis.main_directions: The review emphasizes animal models for safety, immunogenicity, and efficacy, noting their predictive value depends on infection pathophysiology, immune mechanisms, and chosen biomarkers, and illustrates combined influenza and COVID-19 models across discovery to late-stage bridging. (A2, A5)
analysis.current_state: It summarizes established innate and adaptive mechanisms—B‑cell/antibody responses, Fc‑mediated functions and glycosylation, T‑cell memory, CD8+ cytotoxicity—and notes emerging systems serology, omics, and AI/ML tools, whose utility hinges on assay standardization and validation. (A3, A6)
analysis.gaps: Common reasons for clinical failure are discussed, highlighting that many preclinical endpoints lack clear human counterparts or validated surrogate/mechanistic readouts. (A4)
analysis.future_research: A mechanism‑driven model cascade paired with human‑relevant immunological readouts, together with further validation and standardization of omics and AI/ML assays, is recommended to improve candidate prioritization and lower translational risk. (A7, A6)

analysis.summary_en: Background: Viral vaccine development needs mechanistic insight and translational designs linking preclinical to human data (A1). Main directions: Animal models are crucial but their predictive value varies; influenza and COVID-19 examples show combined model use across development stages (A2, A5). Current state: Known innate/adaptive mechanisms (B‑cell, Fc functions, T‑cell, CD8+) are outlined, with emerging omics/AI tools pending standardization (A3, A6). Gaps: Clinical failures often stem from preclinical endpoints lacking human‑counterpart or validated surrogate readouts (A4). Future research: Implement mechanism‑driven model cascades with human‑relevant readouts and validate new assay platforms to reduce translational risk (A7, A6).

title: Structural basis of membrane engagement and polyreactivity control in HIV-1 MPER broadly neutralizing antibodies.

title: Utility of Fine Needle Aspiration Supernatant for Real‐Time PCR –Based Mutation Analysis in Non–Small Cell Lung Cancer

analysis.background: Personalized therapy and molecular sequencing have transformed management of advanced non‑small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC).
analysis.methods: A prospective study of 31 fine‑needle aspiration (FNA) specimens collected in CytoRich Red, 10% neutral buffered formalin, or 10% bovine serum albumin (BSA) evaluated DNA yield and RT‑PCR for KRAS and/or EGFR mutations; DNA was extracted with the QIAamp DNA FFPE Tissue Kit and RT‑PCR performed with QIAGEN therascreen EGFR or KRAS RGQ kits.
analysis.results: In the CytoRich Red group (11 specimens) all results matched standard controls; the formalin group (12 specimens) had nine concordant results, six required repeat extraction and one remained invalid; the BSA group (8 specimens) yielded five concordant results, with three failing PCR pre‑tests despite repeat extraction.
analysis.contribution: The study shows that CytoRich Red supernatant enables reliable RT‑PCR‑based mutation testing, suggesting FNA supernatant can be a practical alternative specimen for lung‑cancer molecular analysis and may preserve cell‑block material.
analysis.limitations: The cohort is small and the evidence is limited to the abstract; detailed demographic, clinical, or performance metrics beyond those reported are not available.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Personalized therapy and molecular sequencing have transformed NSCLC management. Methods: A prospective study of 31 FNA specimens in three media assessed DNA yield and RT‑PCR for KRAS/EGFR using QIAamp extraction and QIAGEN therascreen kits. Results: CytoRich Red (11 specimens) gave 100% concordance; formalin (12) gave nine concordant results with six repeat extractions and one invalid; BSA (8) gave five concordant results with three PCR failures despite repeat extraction. Contribution: CytoRich Red supernatant reliably supports RT‑PCR mutation testing, offering a practical alternative that preserves cell‑block material. Limitations: Small cohort and abstract‑only data limit generalizability.

title: Association of ulinastatin with 28-day mortality across different severities of viral pneumonia: a multicenter propensity score-matched study.

analysis.background: The study addresses hyperinflammation as a key driver of mortality in severe or critical viral pneumonia, particularly COVID‑19 and influenza.
analysis.methods: A multicenter, retrospective cohort of adult ICU patients with confirmed SARS‑CoV‑2 or influenza infection was evaluated; 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) was used to control confounding.
analysis.results: In the matched cohort of 194 patients, 28‑day all‑cause mortality was 29.9% in the ulinastatin group versus 29.9% in controls (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.43‑1.12, p = 0.128). Subgroup analysis showed a significant survival benefit in critically ill patients (HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.30‑0.87, p = 0.011) but not in severe patients (HR 1.48, 95% CI 0.45‑4.85, p = 0.513). The benefit was consistent across COVID‑19 and influenza etiologies (P for interaction = 0.313).
analysis.contribution: The findings suggest that ulinastatin may confer a survival advantage specifically in critically ill viral pneumonia patients, highlighting the potential for precision immunomodulation and the need for targeted therapeutic windows.
analysis.limitations: Not reported in the supplied evidence.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Hyperinflammation drives mortality in severe or critical viral pneumonia, notably COVID‑19 and influenza. Methods: A multicenter, retrospective ICU cohort of adults with confirmed SARS‑CoV‑2 or influenza was analyzed; 1:1 propensity score matching controlled confounding. Results: In 194 matched patients, 28‑day mortality was 29.9% with ulinastatin versus 29.9% without (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.43‑1.12, p = 0.128). Critically ill patients benefited (HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.30‑0.87, p = 0.011), whereas severe patients did not (HR 1.48, 95% CI 0.45‑4.85, p = 0.513); the effect was consistent across COVID‑19 and influenza. Contribution: The study indicates a potential survival benefit of ulinastatin in critically ill viral pneumonia, underscoring precision immunomodulation. Limitations: Not reported in the supplied evidence.

title: Serum lipidome remodeling in viral pneumonia: from pathophysiology to therapeutics.

analysis.background: Viral pneumonia remains a leading global health threat, often culminating in ARDS and systemic organ failure. (A1)
analysis.main_directions: The review reframes viral pneumonia as a systemic metabolic crisis characterized by extensive remodeling of the host lipidome. (A2)
analysis.current_state: Meta‑synthesis of clinical and mechanistic data reveals a "metabolic crash" with sharp LDL‑cholesterol decline and conversion of HDL into a pro‑inflammatory carrier, both serving as decisive prognostic indicators. (A3)
analysis.gaps: The exact mechanisms by which respiratory viruses hijack the SREBP‑SCAP axis and trigger ferroptotic cell death through GPX4‑lipid‑peroxidase exhaustion are still incompletely understood. (A4)
analysis.future_research: Future work should test lipid‑homeostasis restoration via specialized pro‑resolving mediators, metabolic stabilizers, and AI‑driven metabolic endotyping to enable host‑directed precision therapies. (A6, A7)

analysis.summary_en: Background: Viral pneumonia remains a leading global health threat, often leading to ARDS and organ failure. Main directions: The review redefines it as a systemic metabolic crisis with profound lipidome remodeling. Current state: Evidence shows a metabolic crash marked by LDL loss and HDL conversion, serving as prognostic markers. Gaps: How viruses exploit the SREBP‑SCAP pathway and induce ferroptosis via GPX4 depletion is not fully resolved. Future research: Testing lipid‑homeostasis restoration with pro‑resolving mediators, metabolic stabilizers, and AI‑driven endotyping is recommended.

title: Clinical outcomes of bronchodilator use in bronchiolitis: an evidence-based perspective.

analysis.background: Bronchiolitis is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract infection in infants, most commonly due to RSV, and contributes substantially to global pediatric morbidity.
analysis.main_directions: The review evaluates the clinical efficacy of bronchodilators, particularly salbutamol, in bronchiolitis, linking therapeutic rationale to disease pathophysiology.
analysis.current_state: Meta‑analyses of randomized trials indicate no significant benefit of bronchodilators on oxygen saturation, hospitalization rates, length of stay, or time to illness resolution.
analysis.gaps: A persistent gap exists between evidence‑based guidelines discouraging routine bronchodilator use and ongoing clinical practice, reflecting implementation challenges.
analysis.future_research: Research should focus on implementation studies to align practice with guidelines and further characterize safety and physiological effects of bronchodilators in infants.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Bronchiolitis is a leading cause of lower respiratory infection in infants, mainly RSV, driving high pediatric morbidity. Main directions: The review assesses bronchodilator, especially salbutamol, efficacy in bronchiolitis. Current state: Meta‑analyses show no meaningful improvement in key clinical outcomes. Gaps: Evidence‑practice disconnect persists, with routine use still observed. Future research: Implementation studies and safety assessments are needed to align care with guidelines.

title: The Role of CC10 Combined With CysLTs in Predicting Subsequent Wheezing in RSV-Infected Bronchiolitis.

analysis.background: The objective was to clarify the predictive role of club cell 10‑kDa protein (CC10) and cysteinyl leukotrienes (CysLTs) for subsequent wheezing after RSV infection.
analysis.methods: Children hospitalized with RSV‑induced bronchiolitis between 1 Oct 2022 and 31 Oct 2023 were enrolled; nasopharyngeal aspirates were obtained on admission; age‑matched healthy children without respiratory infection served as controls; CC10 and CysLTs levels in NPAs were measured and correlated with disease severity; follow‑up assessments recorded subsequent wheezing.
analysis.results: The study included 169 RSV‑bronchiolitis infants and 22 controls; CC10 levels were lower in the RSV group (219.4 ± 83.1 pg/mL) than controls (284.1 ± 68.1 pg/mL); CC10 and CysLTs levels correlated with disease severity; only CysLTs, together with allergy history and ventilation duration, showed a suggestive link to later wheezing, though further validation is needed.
analysis.contribution: Demonstrates that CC10 and CysLTs are severity biomarkers for RSV bronchiolitis and suggests CysLTs may help predict post‑RSV wheezing, guiding future biomarker and clinical research.
analysis.limitations: Findings are based on an abstract only, control sample size is limited, and the predictive association requires further validation.

analysis.summary_en: Background: The objective was to clarify the predictive role of CC10 and CysLTs for subsequent wheezing after RSV infection. title: Enhancing public health surveillance: A statistical validation of potential sampling bias in large retrospective vaccine cohorts.

analysis.background: Massive administrative datasets are essential for global health surveillance but can conceal systemic selection biases.
analysis.methods: The author audited a retrospective cohort of 2,975,035 individuals linking COVID-19 vaccination to oncological outcomes, benchmarking its composition against national demographic and epidemiological standards using single-proportion Z‑tests.

When revaccination is recommended: An evaluation of non-guideline poliovirus serology testing in Alberta, Canada

analysis.background: NACI advises against routine poliovirus serology testing and recommends revaccination when immunity is unknown.
analysis.methods: POLV serology request data from May 1 2023 to Dec 31 2024 were extracted from a provincial laboratory information system and analyzed for patient demographics, physician specialty and experience, testing indications, vaccine‑record availability, and co‑ordered serologies.
analysis.results: 108 requests from 77 general‑practice physicians (median patient age 34.5 y) were reviewed; 2.8% (3) were POLV‑S alone, 97.2% (105) included a median of 7 additional serologies (measles, rubella, mumps IgG in ~90%); patient history was missing in 79.6% (86); testing was mainly for employment (45.5%), occupational health forms (27.3%), immigration (13.6%) and immunity verification (13.6%); vaccine records existed for 46.3% (50) patients, of whom 56% lacked a POLV vaccine date.
analysis.contribution: The authors highlight substantial non‑adherence to NACI guidelines and propose education on revaccination and limited utility of POLV serology to improve laboratory efficiency and ensure immunity.
analysis.limitations: Only the abstract is available, limiting detail on study design, statistical analysis, and broader context.

analysis.summary_en: Background: NACI advises against routine poliovirus serology testing, recommending revaccination when immunity is unknown. Methods: Provincial lab data (May 2023–Dec 2024) on POLV serology requests were analyzed for demographics, physician details, indications, vaccine records, and co‑ordered tests. Results: Among 108 requests from 77 general‑practice physicians (median age 34.5 y), 2.8% were POLV‑S alone; 97.2% included ~7 other serologies (≈90% measles, rubella, mumps IgG); 79.6% lacked patient history; main reasons were employment (45.5%), occupational health (27.3%), immigration (13.6%), immunity verification (13.6%); vaccine records were present for 46.3% of patients, 56% of whom lacked POLV vaccine dates. Limitations: Only the abstract is provided, restricting detail on methods and analysis.

title: Demographic and Clinical Determinants of Acute Bronchiolitis Outcomes in a Tertiary Pediatric Hospital in Dubai, United Arab Emirates

analysis.background: Bronchiolitis causes significant morbidity in children under two, especially in winter, yet demographic and clinical determinants in Middle Eastern populations are poorly described.
analysis.methods: Retrospective review of infants 1‑24 months admitted with bronchiolitis Oct 2022‑Mar 2023 at a tertiary pediatric hospital; extracted age, sex, nationality, gestational age, feeding, atopy history, viral PCR, oxygen saturation, therapies; primary outcomes were PICU admission, maximum oxygen support, and length of stay; associations tested with chi‑square/Fisher and Mann‑Whitney U (p < 0.05).
analysis.results: From 1,804 encounters, 232 met criteria (mean age 6.6 ± 5.2 mo, 59.5% male). RSV detected in 43.5%, rhinovirus/enterovirus 12.5%, mixed/other 22.8%. High‑flow nasal cannula used in 37.5%; PICU admission 6.1%. No demographic or clinical factor significantly affected PICU or oxygen requirement; family history of atopy associated with shorter stay; steroids given more often to those needing higher oxygen but did not reduce PICU or shorten stay.
analysis.contribution: Bronchiolitis outcomes in this UAE cohort appear largely independent of demographics, viral etiology, or corticosteroid use, supporting guideline‑based supportive care and discouraging routine steroid or bronchodilator use to improve resource utilization.
analysis.limitations: Not reported in the supplied evidence.

title: Unrecognized Dengue Transmission in Socially Vulnerable Peri-Urban Neighborhoods of a Temperate Argentine City: Integrating Serology with Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices

analysis.background: Dengue is an emerging arboviral disease in temperate South America, where urban expansion, climate variability, and social vulnerability favor transmission.
analysis.methods: Cross‑sectional study of 188 adults in three socioeconomically vulnerable peripheral neighborhoods of Santa Fe, Argentina, conducted Dec 2019–Mar 2020, assessing anti‑DENV IgG by ELISA and collecting KAP questionnaires with peridomiciliary observations.
analysis.results: Apparent seropositivity was 16.5% (adjusted 10.7% after test‑performance correction); most seropositive individuals had no prior dengue diagnosis; dengue awareness was high (98.4%) but knowledge was incomplete and weakly linked to preventive practices; multivariate analysis found higher odds of seropositivity for residents living farther from vacant lots.
analysis.contribution: Shows substantial unrecognized dengue circulation and illustrates that integrating serology with KAP surveys provides actionable insight for targeted surveillance and public‑health interventions in vulnerable urban settings.
analysis.limitations: Only abstract information is available; detailed methodology, sample‑size justification, and broader contextual data are not reported.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Dengue is emerging in temperate South America, driven by urban growth, climate variability, and social vulnerability. Methods: A cross‑sectional survey of 188 adults in three peri‑urban, vulnerable neighborhoods of Santa Fe, Argentina (Dec 2019–Mar 2020) measured anti‑DENV IgG by ELISA and collected KAP questionnaires with peridomiciliary observations. Results: Apparent seropositivity was 16.5% (adjusted 10.7%); most seropositive persons lacked prior diagnosis; awareness was 98.4% but knowledge was incomplete and weakly linked to practices; living farther from vacant lots increased odds of seropositivity. Contribution: Highlights hidden dengue transmission and shows that combining serology with KAP data can guide targeted surveillance and interventions in vulnerable urban areas. Limitations: Findings are based solely on abstract data; detailed methods and broader context are not reported.

title: An evaluation of cytokine responses and antiseizure medication levels during mild upper respiratory infections in children with epilepsy

analysis.background: The study aimed to investigate whether mild upper respiratory tract infections affect serum antiseizure medication levels and inflammation in children with idiopathic epilepsy.
analysis.methods: Forty‑nine children aged 2–18 years on valproate (n=31) or carbamazepine (n=18) were evaluated at infection onset and one month later; serum drug levels, IL‑17A, IL‑23, CBC, liver and kidney function, albumin, ESR, CRP, and EEG were measured.
analysis.results: No provoked seizures occurred during infection. Valproate levels were higher during infection but not significantly (p=0.073); carbamazepine levels showed no significant change (p=0.484). IL‑23 increased significantly during infection in carbamazepine users (p=0.039) but not in valproate users.
analysis.contribution: The findings suggest that mild upper respiratory infections do not produce clinically significant alterations in serum valproate or carbamazepine concentrations, informing clinical management of epilepsy during infections.
analysis.limitations: Not reported in the supplied evidence.

title: Serology and molecular genetic analysis of weakened expression of ABO blood group antigens in Chinese pediatric population.

analysis.background: The ABO blood group system is vital for red blood cell antigens, and weakened expression can lead to misidentification of blood types.
analysis.methods: Blood samples from 44 pediatric cases underwent serological analysis by microcolumn agglutination and tube tests; promoter and exons 1‑7 of the ABO gene were sequenced; missense variants were evaluated with PolyPhen‑2; pedigree analysis was performed on four cases.
analysis.results: Eighteen different ABO subgroup alleles were detected, including 7 subtype A (mainly A2), 7 subtype B (Bw, B3), one cisAB and three B(A); observed phenotypes were A2, Bw, B3, A2B, ABw, AB3, cisAB and B(A); a rare B allele c.538C>T (p.Arg180Cys) had a PolyPhen‑2 score of 1.00, and pedigree analysis supported autosomal inheritance.
analysis.contribution: The study highlights that ABO genotyping is essential for accurate blood group identification and transfusion safety in young children.
analysis.limitations: Only an abstract is available; detailed methodology, statistical analysis, and broader population data are not reported.

analysis.summary_en: Background: The ABO system is vital and weakened expression can cause blood type misidentification. Methods: 44 pediatric cases were serologically tested, ABO gene promoter and exons sequenced, variants assessed with PolyPhen‑2, and pedigrees of four cases analyzed. Results: 18 subgroup alleles were found (7 A2, 7 B subtypes, 1 cisAB, 3 B(A)), with phenotypes A2, Bw, B3, A2B, ABw, AB3, cisAB, B(A); a rare B allele c.538C>T (p.Arg180Cys) scored 1.00 on PolyPhen‑2 and showed autosomal inheritance. Contribution: Demonstrates the necessity of ABO genotyping for accurate typing and transfusion safety in children. Limitations: Only abstract provided; detailed methods and broader data not reported.

title: Clinical characteristics and associated factors of post-infectious bronchiolitis obliterans in children with severe pneumonia and respiratory failure: a retrospective cohort study

analysis.background: Post-infectious bronchiolitis obliterans (PIBO) is a severe sequela of severe pneumonia in children (F1) and data on its occurrence among those with concurrent respiratory failure are limited (F2).
analysis.methods: A retrospective analysis of 108 children with severe pneumonia and respiratory failure from Jan 2015 to Jun 2025 was performed (F4); patients were classified into PIBO (n=52) and non‑PIBO (n=56) groups (F5) and clinical, etiologic, imaging, and treatment variables were compared, with additional age‑stratified (<2 yr vs ≥2 yr) analysis (F6).
analysis.results: PIBO prevalence was 48.1% (52/108) (F7). Compared with non‑PIBO, the PIBO group had longer fever (median 17 vs 7 days, P<0.001) (F8), more wheezing (86.5% vs 58.9%, P=0.001) (F9), higher adenovirus detection (65.6% vs lower) (F10), higher invasive ventilation use (61.5% vs 19.6%, P<0.001) (F12), longer ICU stay (median 14 vs 6 days, P<0.001) (F13) and hospitalization (median 28 vs 15 days, P<0.001) (F14). Age‑stratified analysis showed prolonged fever and invasive ventilation remained significantly associated with PIBO in both age groups (P<0.05) (F11). No difference in atopic disease history (F16); non‑PIBO had more liver impairment, consolidation, and patchy exudation (F17‑F19).
analysis.contribution: The study identifies prolonged fever, adenovirus infection, and critical‑illness indicators (invasive ventilation, ICU support) as factors associated with later PIBO, informing targeted long‑term follow‑up and early assessment in high‑risk children (F20,F21).
analysis.limitations: Not reported in the supplied evidence.

analysis.summary_en: Background: PIBO is a severe sequela of severe pneumonia in children, with limited data on occurrence in those with respiratory failure. Methods: Retrospective cohort of 108 children (2015‑2025) divided into PIBO (n=52) and non‑PIBO (n=56) groups; clinical and laboratory data compared, with age‑stratified analysis. Results: PIBO prevalence was 48.1%; associated with longer fever, higher wheezing, adenovirus detection, invasive ventilation, and longer ICU/hospital stays; associations held across age groups.
